summary: This guide outlines the steps to set up an OAuth 2.0 application for Linear to read issues from a user's workspace, covering application registration, user authorization, token exchange, and API requests.

effort.handsOn: Estimate: 30-60 min; assumes an existing backend for handling redirects and token exchange.
effort.basis: Based on typical OAuth application setup and integration timeframes, assuming developer familiarity with OAuth flows.

prerequisites.title: Linear Account
prerequisites.detail: A Linear account is required to create and manage OAuth applications.

prerequisites.title: Backend Server
prerequisites.detail: A backend server capable of handling OAuth redirects and securely storing client secrets is necessary for the authorization code flow.

permissions.name: read
permissions.reason: This scope grants read access to the user's account, which is necessary to read issues from their workspace. It is a default scope.

steps.title: Register OAuth Application
steps.action: Create a new OAuth2 application in Linear's developer settings.
steps.detail: Navigate to your Linear developer settings and register a new OAuth2 application. You will need to provide an application name and a redirect URI. This process will provide you with a `client_id` and `client_secret`.
steps.successCheck: You have obtained a `client_id` and `client_secret` for your application.
steps.recovery: If you encounter issues, review the Linear OAuth documentation or check your application settings for errors.

steps.title: Configure Redirect URI
steps.action: Set up your application's redirect URI.
steps.detail: Ensure the `redirect_uri` configured in your Linear OAuth application matches the endpoint on your server that will handle the authorization code. This URI must be HTTPS.
steps.successCheck: The redirect URI is correctly configured in Linear and on your server.
steps.recovery: Verify the redirect URI in your Linear app settings and ensure your server endpoint is correctly configured to receive the authorization code.

steps.title: Initiate User Authorization
steps.action: Redirect users to Linear's authorization URL.
steps.detail: Construct an authorization URL using your `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `response_type=code`, and `scope=read`. Redirect your users to `https://linear.app/oauth/authorize`. Include a `state` parameter for CSRF protection.
steps.successCheck: The user is redirected to Linear's consent screen and, upon approval, back to your `redirect_uri` with an authorization `code`.
steps.recovery: Check your authorization URL parameters for correctness. Ensure the `redirect_uri` is registered and accessible.

steps.title: Exchange Code for Tokens
steps.action: Exchange the authorization code for an access token.
steps.detail: Upon receiving the authorization `code` at your `redirect_uri`, make a POST request to `https://api.linear.app/oauth/token`. Include the `code`, `redirect_uri`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, and `grant_type=authorization_code` in the request body. This will return an `access_token` and `refresh_token`.
steps.successCheck: Your server successfully receives an `access_token` and `refresh_token`.
steps.recovery: Verify all parameters in your POST request. Ensure your `client_secret` is correct and securely handled. Check server logs for any errors from Linear's token endpoint.

steps.title: Read User Issues
steps.action: Make an API request to read issues using the access token.
steps.detail: Use the obtained `access_token` to make a GraphQL API request to `https://api.linear.app/graphql`. Include the token in the `Authorization` header as `Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>`. First, query the `viewer` to confirm authentication, then query for team IDs, and finally fetch issues for a specific team.
steps.successCheck: You successfully retrieve issue data from the user's workspace.
steps.recovery: If the API request fails, check the `access_token` for validity and expiration. Ensure the `Authorization` header is correctly formatted. Review Linear's GraphQL API documentation for query syntax.

steps.title: Switch Application Distribution to Public
steps.action: Change your application's distribution setting to 'public'.
steps.detail: By default, Linear OAuth applications are private and only work within the workspace where they were created. To make your application available to other workspaces, you must switch its distribution to `public`.
steps.successCheck: Your application's distribution status is set to 'public'.
steps.recovery: If you cannot find the setting, consult Linear's developer documentation or support. Ensure you are in the correct developer settings for your application.

agentBrief: Set up a Linear OAuth 2.0 application to read user issues. You will need to register an application in Linear's developer settings (https://linear.app/settings/api) to obtain a `client_id` and `client_secret`. Configure a `redirect_uri` on your backend to handle the authorization code. The user will be redirected to `https://linear.app/oauth/authorize` for consent. Your backend will then exchange the received code for an `access_token` at `https://api.linear.app/oauth/token`. Finally, use this token to make GraphQL API calls to `https://api.linear.app/graphql` to read issues. Remember to switch the application's distribution to 'public' (https://linear.app/developers/oauth-app-manifests) for broader availability. Human authorization is required for application registration and any account changes.

request.useCase: Read issues from a user workspace
